answer: To mitigate fake-identity attacks, an economy of AI agents can employ a mechanism known as "Timber Island Voting", where each agent is assigned a unique, publicly-verifiable digital identity tied to a cryptographic hash of its computational resources. An attacker attempting to forge a new identity can only do so by incurring a significant computational cost, akin to felling a large timber, rendering it economically unviable. Meanwhile, legitimate agents can vote without fear of impersonation, ensuring the integrity of the consensus network.
